notes: Manifest has no runtime dependency on any other Cognous component: no imports, no fetches, no sha checks in code. Peer coupling is (a) the Alvorada commit/profile ids in docs and in the example manifest metadata and profile_ref, (b) the shared canonical JSON/digest algorithm, (c) a shared, unspecified reason-code vocabulary, (d) the const '0.1.0' Authority Context schema_version.

The Alvorada pin is embedded inside a digest-covered artifact (examples/refund_integration_v1_1.manifest.json:143 metadata). Because manifest_digest covers metadata, any peer bump changes manifest_digest and invalidates previously issued proposals/decisions; decoupling needs the pin moved out of metadata or excluded from the digest.

The Control Plane duplicates proposal_mismatches rather than calling it, and diverges: CP never runs validate_manifest, ignores tools[].allowed (E015) and default_action, and never reads authority_context.evidence_obligation_ids or schema_version; CP's consumed fixture is a byte-identical copy of this repo's example (diff verified). Divergence risk is unguarded by any shared conformance vector.

Proposal wire format: RuntimeActionProposalV12 has no generation/discriminator field and the schema still pins manifest_version const '1.1' (schemas/runtime_action_proposal_v1_2.schema.json:33); '1.2' exists only in description/docstring (schema line 5, models.py:332). Consumers must pick the class out-of-band.

docs/integrations and schemas disclaim equivalence: Python models are looser than JSON schemas (docs/manifest_format.md:178-187), so 'valid per aam' does not imply schema-valid; the Control Plane validates neither.

examples/runtime_action_proposal_v1_2.json uses manifest_id 'urn:cognous:manifest:synthetic-refund-v1' (line 3) while the fixture manifest_id is 'refund-integration-pilot-v1'; its manifest_digest matches the fixture digest, so the sample would yield manifest_id_mismatch if run through proposal_mismatches.
